semanticTokens.pageDescription: Choose color, surface, type, and layer tokens by the object you are designing.
semanticTokens.quickStartBody: First decide what you are coloring, then choose the matching token. Do not start with a color value.
semanticTokens.backgroundsChoiceBody: Backgrounds for pages, cards, menus, and dialogs.
semanticTokens.textChoiceBody: Body copy, supporting text, links, and icons that inherit text color.
semanticTokens.actionsChoiceBody: Primary actions, secondary actions, and persistent selection.
semanticTokens.boundariesChoiceBody: Dividers, input boundaries, and visible focus indication.
semanticTokens.feedbackChoiceBody: Information that communicates success, risk, error, warning, or guidance.
semanticTokens.commonRecipesBody: An interface element usually needs a set of tokens, not a single color. Use these combinations directly.
semanticTokens.actionFillBody: Use these fills for buttons, inverse actions, and clear selection. Pair text or icons with the corresponding on token.
semanticTokens.foregroundBody: For text and icons on ordinary page, card, and menu backgrounds. The color level reflects content importance, not font size.
semanticTokens.onPairBody: on means “placed on a specific fill”. For example, use fg-on-brand only with brand, brand-hover, or brand-active—not on page or card backgrounds.
semanticTokens.surfaceBody: A Surface is the background that carries content. Choose it by where the container sits—from page to card, menu, and dialog—not by component name.
semanticTokens.boundariesBody: Use border for ordinary dividers, input for input and selection controls, and the independent focus-ring for visible focus. Action controls normally show it for keyboard focus, while text-editing controls may also show it after pointer focus according to :focus-visible.
semanticTokens.interactionBody: hover is temporary feedback on hover; active is temporary feedback while pressed, dragged, or expanded; selection is persistent selection.
semanticTokens.feedbackBody: Do not communicate status by changing text color alone. Combine its background, text or icon, and border.
semanticTokens.supportBody: These colors support internal details such as transparent checkerboards. Do not use them in interface designs or component selection.
semanticTokens.developerReferenceBody: Use the material below to match Figma design tokens with CSS variables, Tailwind utilities, and source files. Designers can skip it.
semanticTokens.ledgerBody: Each name is the design token and the Figma variable name. Theme modes change values; the design vocabulary stays stable.
semanticTokens.namingBody: Figma paths stay unchanged, for example surface/floating. CSS custom properties and Tailwind utilities are implementation details, not a second naming system to learn.
